State of Semantic HTML, Page Structure & IA on Top Sites

A first-party audit of 60 pinned Tranco top-500 homepages (list 2026-10-17), comparing what a non-rendering client receives (raw HTML) against a hydrated browser (rendered DOM). Two back-to-back runs, 2 total.

Download dataset (JSON) · Methodology & caveats below.

Headline adoption (raw HTML)

  • Single H1: 31/60
  • Valid heading sequence (no skipped levels): 22/60
  • Multiple H1: 5/60
  • JSON-LD present: 20/60
  • Canonical link: 31/60
  • OG title: 40/60 · OG image: 37/60
  • Viewport meta: 50/60 · lang attribute: 46/60
  • Skip-to-main link: 12/60
  • Semantic ratio (landmark tags / total elements) median: 0.0078
  • Images missing alt: 36/1238

Rendered counts are higher — structure that non-rendering AI crawlers (which execute no JavaScript) never see.

Methodology & caveats

  • Sample: 60 of the first 60 entries of Tranco list 64VVX, infrastructure domains filtered.
  • Two passes per homepage with the same user agent — plain HTTP parse (JS-disabled context) vs. headless Chromium — so JavaScript execution is the only variable.
  • Signals extracted: landmark counts, heading hierarchy, JSON-LD types, meta/OG, alt text, links, images, tables, breadcrumbs, FAQ signals, skip links.
  • Homepage only; deep-page (money-page) pass is in progress and will extend breadcrumbs/tables/FAQ adoption numbers.
  • Token-set overlap is an upper bound; anti-bot/consent interstitials confound both passes.
  • Two back-to-back runs; 56/59 sites stable within 0.001 on semantic ratio.
